mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A's FOR shots and FOR shots_on_target (both all-prior and recent-5 windows) alongside Team B's AGAINST shots and AGAINST shots_on_target. The mechanism requires the joint relationship between volume and accuracy across both sides simultaneously — not either observable alone against a single band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shots_on_target FOR rate declines relative to its all-prior rate while the opponent's shots_on_target AGAINST rate is also below competition baseline, the match-level shots_on_target total is suppressed relative to what either team's individual baseline would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots FOR vs shots_on_target FOR) is jointly compared against Team B's defensive suppression of both shots and shots_on_target allowed, to test whether a high-volume but recently declining accuracy attacker facing a low-shots-allowed defence produces a jointly suppressed shots_on_target outcome relative to each team's individual baselines.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint product of two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) across both FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to one observable mirrored against its opponent-allowed counterpart, nor to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the cross-team asymmetry: Team A FOR fouls (low, ~11) vs Team A AGAINST fouls (high, ~14.4, spiking to 16 recently) combined with Team B AGAINST fouls (low all-prior ~12.7, spiking to 16 recently). The joint signal is the simultaneous divergence of both teams' recent AGAINST-fouls from their all-prior baselines, not either team's foul rate alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams show a recent spike in fouls-AGAINST relative to their all-prior baselines, total match fouls and yellow cards rise above what either team's individual all-prior foul rate would predict, with the asymmetry (one team draws fouls, the other commits them) amplifying card accumulation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's asymmetric foul-production profile (low fouls FOR, high fouls AGAINST) is jointly conditioned with Team B's recent spike in fouls AGAINST to test whether a match where one side commits few fouls but draws many, facing an opponent whose opponents have recently fouled them more, produces an elevated total-fouls and yellow-cards outcome beyond what either team's individual foul rate predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams' FOR and AGAINST perspectives simultaneously, plus a recent-vs-all-prior divergence on both sides at once. It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team A FOR possession (all-prior ~54, home ~55) and Team B FOR possession away (~47 vs home ~51), alongside both teams' corner FOR and AGAINST rates split by half (first-half vs second-half). The mechanism requires the joint interaction of possession asymmetry and its half-level translation into corners — two distinct observables across two venue-split dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A holds a structural possession advantage that is amplified by Team B's away-venue possession drop, Team A's corner-kick generation rises above its all-prior average, and the corner differential between the two teams widens beyond what either team's individual corner rate or possession rate alone would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team A's possession dominance (FOR possession well above 50) and Team B's away possession deficit (away possession notably below home possession) is tested against corner-kick generation: specifically whether Team A's possession advantage, when compounded by Team B's structural away-possession drop, produces a corner-kick differential that exceeds what either team's individual corner baseline predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) where the conditioning involves two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue-split possession for both teams) and a half-level resolution for corners. It cannot be reduced to one observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-vs-all-prior divergence for both teams simultaneously: Team A FOR goals (recent-5 ~1.0 vs all-prior ~1.9) and Team B AGAINST goals (recent-5 ~2.2 vs all-prior ~1.56), combined with Team A AGAINST goals (recent-5 ~2.2 vs all-prior ~1.31) and Team B FOR goals (recent-5 ~0.8 vs all-prior ~1.47). The mechanism tests whether the cross-product of these four divergences — two teams each showing recent-form shifts in both attack and defence — produces a non-additive total-goals signal.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams simultaneously show a recent-form divergence from their all-prior goal rates (one team's attack declining while both teams' defences are conceding more recently), the total goals outcome diverges from the competition baseline in a direction that is not predictable from any single team's recent or all-prior rate alone, suggesting a threshold or regime shift in the joint recent-form signal.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's recent-form goal-scoring collapse (FOR goals recent-5 well below all-prior) is jointly conditioned with Team B's recent defensive deterioration (AGAINST goals recent-5 above all-prior) to test whether the simultaneous divergence of both teams' recent goal rates from their long-run baselines — in opposite directions — produces a goals total that is non-linearly different from what either team's all-prior rate or the competition baseline would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint conditioning on four recent-vs-all-prior divergences across both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates simultaneously. It is not a single observable with a recent-vs-long-run split, nor a single observable with one opponent band — it requires the cross-product of both teams' simultaneous form divergences.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B FOR red_cards away (~0.216) vs home (~0.125), Team A AGAINST red_cards recent-5 (~0.4 vs all-prior ~0.182), and both teams' cards_2h rates (second-half card accumulation). The mechanism requires the joint interaction of two distinct observables (red_cards and cards_2h) across two venue-split and temporal dimensions simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's away red-card rate is structurally elevated above its home rate, and Team A's recent AGAINST red-card rate has spiked above its all-prior level, the second-half card total (cards_2h) rises above competition baseline, with the joint signal being stronger than either team's individual card rate would predict in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: The joint relationship between Team B's elevated away red-card rate (away red cards FOR notably above home) and Team A's elevated red-cards-AGAINST rate (recent-5 spiking above all-prior), conditioned on second-half card accumulation rates for both teams, is tested to determine whether the combination of Team B's away disciplinary risk and Team A's recent tendency to provoke red cards produces a second-half cards total that exceeds competition baseline beyond what either team's individual card rate predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a joint relationship between two distinct observables (red_cards and cards_2h) conditioned on two opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue split for Team B's red cards, and recent-vs-all-prior for Team A's AGAINST red cards), plus a within-match temporal split (second half). It is not reducible to one observable with one conditioning band.
